ro.effect: hard stop

bestPractice: STOP before any other question. Say why and point to the GP. Check date of birth again at the ID step.
source: Every licence is 18+ (clinical-men 10.2; clinical-women 1.11 item 7 and 4.1 Q1); verify DOB with ID (uk-regulation 6.2).

treated.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged)? (limit 49 for fin, Regaine)

ro.effect: men none; women 66+ removes oral minoxidil

bestPractice: No stop. Route to the clinician. Topical minoxidil over 65 is off-label: record why and tell the GP. Oral minoxidil only after a real blood pressure and pulse reading; set and publish a service age limit for it.
source: Men's 5% solution licensed 18-65, men's foam 18-49 (clinical-men 3.1); women's products 18-65 (clinical-women 3.0, 4.1 Q1); oral minoxidil SmPC: few studies over 65, risk of dizziness on standing (clinical-women 3.2 'Older women').

situation: Woman (female at birth) on a men's route

hims-uk.effect: hard stop; sent to Hers UK

hair-and-me.effect: re-routed by sex at birth; no 5-ARI

ro.effect: sent to women's visit

bestPractice: Switch her to the women's pathway (do not just stop). Never offer finasteride, dutasteride or a men's 5% minoxidil solution.
source: Finasteride and dutasteride contraindicated in women; men's 5% solutions contraindicated in women (clinical-women 3.1, 3.4; key facts 17, 24).

situation: Woman pregnant, breastfeeding or trying to conceive

voy.effect: hard stop likely; TTC removes oral minoxidil

hers-us.effect: removes oral minoxidil, removes finasteride and dutasteride products, −spiro

ro.effect: pregnant hard stop; breastfeeding removes oral minoxidil, topical kept

happy-head.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) 'critical'; nothing removed

bestPractice: No medicine at all: advice and safe scalp care only. Re-ask at every supply.
source: Topical minoxidil 'should not be used during pregnancy or lactation'; oral minoxidil, spironolactone and 5-ARIs contraindicated or avoided (clinical-women 3.12 and 4.1 Q2).

situation: Woman who could conceive and uses no contraception

happy-head.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged); spironolactone + oral minoxidil kept

bestPractice: Exclude spironolactone and oral minoxidil until effective contraception is in place. Ask again at every supply.
source: clinical-women 3.2, 3.3 and 4.1 Q3; key fact 23 (anti-androgens can feminise a male fetus).

situation: Man whose partner is pregnant (or a pregnant person at home)

hims-uk.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) or removes finasteride and dutasteride products expected

hims-us.effect: handling warning or flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged)

ro.effect: not asked

happy-head.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged); 'do not accept' keeps dutasteride

bestPractice: Tablets: carry on, with 'do not let her handle crushed or broken tablets'. Dutasteride: condom while she is or may be pregnant. Topical finasteride or dutasteride: counsel on skin transfer, or choose another product.
source: Semen exposure judged unlikely to harm (finasteride SmPC); dutasteride SmPC condom advice; topical products absorbed through skin (clinical-men 2.1, 2.3 and 10.2 table).

hims-uk.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) or removes finasteride and dutasteride products expected

hair-and-me.effect: not asked; leaflet removes finasteride and dutasteride products

boots-online-doctor.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) ('Danger' flag)

ro.effect: removes finasteride and dutasteride products from recommendation + caution

bestPractice: Clinician discussion, not a silent removal. Avoid dutasteride (weeks-long half-life, sperm effects persist). Finasteride: shared decision; offer minoxidil-only if he prefers.
source: clinical-men 2.1 (fertility data are from 5 mg), 2.3 (dutasteride sperm count still down 24 weeks after stopping), 10.2 table.

situation: Heart disease (heart failure, pericarditis, arrhythmia, angina)

hims-uk.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) or removes all minoxidil products expected

treated.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged); Regaine kept

ro.effect: removes oral minoxidil from recommendation (some conditions)

happy-head.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged); oral kept

bestPractice: No oral minoxidil with past pericardial effusion, tamponade or pericarditis, heart failure, or pulmonary hypertension with mitral stenosis. Arrhythmia or fast pulse: precaution, involve GP or cardiology. Topical minoxidil: medical advice first.
source: Oral minoxidil consensus lists (clinical-men 3.2, 10.2; clinical-women 3.2); topical SmPC 'see a doctor first' (clinical-women 3.1).

sons.effect: removes all minoxidil products (5% spray too)

treated.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged); Regaine kept

boots-online-doctor.effect: bundle: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) ('Danger')

ro.effect: only 'very high': removes oral minoxidil from recommendation

bestPractice: Topical minoxidil: contraindicated (treated or untreated) in the licensed SmPC; prescriber may override only with a recorded reason. Oral minoxidil: verified reading and full BP-medicine list first.
source: Regaine 5% solution SmPC 4.3 (clinical-men 3.1, 10.2); clinical-women 4.1 Q22.

hims-uk.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) expected

ro.effect: no recommendation; all pickable

happy-head.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) 'critical'; oral kept

bestPractice: Below 90/60 or fainting: no oral minoxidil without specialist input. Topical minoxidil is not contraindicated: counsel about dizziness.

hims-uk.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) expected

numan.effect: removes all minoxidil products (via BP answer)

philip-kingsley.effect: free text, no rule reads it

boots-online-doctor.effect: bundle: switch request + flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged)

ro.effect: none (medicines not flagged)

bestPractice: Oral minoxidil only after a clinician has reviewed the full list (doxazosin or 3+ BP drugs: higher drop-out); women's pathway excludes oral minoxidil on BP tablets.

ro.effect: removes oral minoxidil

bestPractice: Never oral minoxidil.
source: Loniten SmPC and consensus contraindication (clinical-men 3.2; clinical-women 3.2).

numan.effect: free text → flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged)

lloyds-online-doctor.effect: eGFR<30 hard stop; else removes oral minoxidil

bestPractice: Ask about kidney disease and, if yes, the latest eGFR. Oral minoxidil: precaution, specialist or GP input. Spironolactone: not with significant kidney impairment.
source: Consensus precaution 'kidney impairment; dialysis' (clinical-men 3.2); Aldactone SmPC (clinical-women 3.3, 4.1 Q24).

sons.effect: severe: removes finasteride and dutasteride products

numan.effect: free text → flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged)

ro.effect: none (even cirrhosis)

bestPractice: Severe liver disease: no dutasteride. Caution with every oral option; discuss with the GP.
source: Avodart SmPC (clinical-men 2.3, 10.2); PCDS severe liver impairment for oral minoxidil (clinical-women 3.2, 4.1 Q25).

situation: Prostate cancer history, or PSA monitoring

hair-and-me.effect: none; leaflet removes finasteride and dutasteride products

numan.effect: PSA: warning only; opt-out not enforced

boots-online-doctor.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) (amber); PSA notice

ro.effect: −spray only; tablets kept

bestPractice: Prostate cancer history: clinician route and GP or urologist agreement before any 5-ARI. PSA monitoring: tell the GP; finasteride halves PSA (SmPC says consider doubling the result).
source: clinical-men 2.1 (PSA), 10.2 table, and verification gap 4 (high-grade prostate cancer wording in the SmPC).

situation: Male breast cancer history, breast lump or gynaecomastia

hair-and-me.effect: none; leaflet removes finasteride and dutasteride products

ro.effect: not asked

bestPractice: Current lump, pain or discharge: STOP and refer to the GP. Past male breast cancer: clinician route, no 5-ARI without specialist agreement.
source: Male breast cancer reported on finasteride (clinical-men 10.2 table).

voy.effect: warning only or flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) likely

sons.effect: low score none; high score removes finasteride and dutasteride products

numan.effect: extra questions + flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged); specialist-led removes finasteride and dutasteride products

philip-kingsley.effect: warning only, then paid consult (minoxidil blocked too)

ro.effect: removes finasteride and dutasteride products from recommendation

bestPractice: Always ask. Do not auto-block minoxidil. Before any 5-ARI: two-way clinician discussion, written mood warning (patient-card wording if compounded), GP letter, review at 2-4 weeks and every visit.
source: MHRA April 2024 and May 2026 (clinical-men 10.1, 10.2; key facts 6-8); dutasteride precautionary warning (clinical-men 2.3).

situation: Suicidal thoughts or self-harm (now or recent)

sons.effect: removes finasteride and dutasteride products silently; no signposting

numan.effect: removes finasteride and dutasteride products; no signposting

happy-head.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) (mental health)

bestPractice: STOP the sale, show crisis help on the same screen (NHS 111, Samaritans, 999), and have a clinician contact the patient. No 5-ARI.
source: clinical-women 4.1 Q11 ('self-harm thoughts: urgent help'); MHRA: stop finasteride at once if suicidal thoughts (clinical-men 10.1, 11).

lloyds-online-doctor.effect: removes finasteride and dutasteride products (ED tablets: removes finasteride and dutasteride products, removes oral minoxidil)

ro.effect: removes finasteride and dutasteride products from recommendation

bestPractice: Ask and record a baseline. Not a contraindication: clinician discussion; offer minoxidil-only if he prefers.
source: Baseline needed because effects can persist (clinical-men 10.2 table); sexual side effects 3.8% vs 2.1% (key fact 5).

keeps.effect: legacy → clinician request; main quiz none

situation: Complete baldness, scars or shiny skin

hims-uk.effect: quiz: none; hard stop likely later

treated.effect: scars: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged)

ro.effect: women: named scarring diagnosis hard stop

bestPractice: Scarring signs: STOP and urgent referral (scarring is permanent). Complete baldness: STOP; medicines do not regrow it.
source: PCDS urgent referral (clinical-women 1.0, 1.11 item 1; key fact 1); treatments not shown to work in complete loss (Voy and Hims leaflets; clinical-men 10.2).

group: E. Type of hair loss and scalp
situation: Scalp pain, redness, infection, psoriasis or eczema

numan.effect: pain/redness removes all minoxidil products; psoriasis flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) only

philip-kingsley.effect: pain or crusting: paid consult; mild itch: scalp plans

treated.effect: itchy scalp: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged)

ro.effect: men: redness no recommendation, pain none; women: diagnosis hard stop

happy-head.effect: free text; flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged)

bestPractice: Pain, burning, pustules, crusting, scale round hairs: STOP and refer. Diagnosed psoriasis or eczema, sunburn, broken skin: no topical minoxidil until settled. Plain dandruff: ketoconazole shampoo, carry on.
source: Topical minoxidil SmPC contraindication (clinical-men 3.1); red flags (clinical-women 1.11 item 1, 4.1 Q5 and Q26); ketoconazole for dandruff (clinical-men 11 step 1).

source: clinical-men 3.1 and key fact 12 (propylene glycol is the usual cause; foam has none).

hair-and-me.effect: none; leaflet removes finasteride and dutasteride products

treated.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) (any allergy)

boots-online-doctor.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) ('other medicines')

bestPractice: No finasteride in any form (tablet, spray, capsule). Dutasteride only after clinician review.

philip-kingsley.effect: free text, no rule reads it

treated.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) (any allergy)

boots-online-doctor.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) ('something else')

bestPractice: Remove propylene-glycol solutions; offer the licensed PG-free foam. Ethanol sensitivity: the foam also contains ethanol, so clinician review.
source: Regaine solution SmPC contraindicates ethanol or propylene glycol sensitivity; formulation table (clinical-men 3.1).

situation: Already taking dutasteride or finasteride 5 mg

hair-and-me.effect: must agree to stop it; leaflet removes finasteride and dutasteride products

philip-kingsley.effect: free text, no rule reads it

bestPractice: No second 5-ARI. Offer minoxidil only, and tell the GP (he is likely under prostate care).
source: 'Do not combine with another 5-alpha reductase inhibitor' (clinical-men 2.1); 'never both' (clinical-men 11 step 3).

numan.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) note; tablets kept

treated.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) (any allergy)

bestPractice: Ask. Hereditary galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption: no lactose-containing tablet; check each brand's excipients.
source: Not covered in the foundations files. The companies' own documents (Boots, Voy, Numan) say finasteride tablets contain lactose; confirm against the SmPC before writing the rule.

ro.effect: not asked

bestPractice: Ask. Warn that topical minoxidil can poison cats (licking skin, pillows, spills); give handling advice; offer an oral option if clinically suitable. Never a reason to stop.
source: customer-voice.md (Cats Protection, May 2026: 20 cat poisonings; PubMed 34370845: 8 of 62 poisoned cats died).

situation: Babies or young children who touch the scalp or pillow
bestPractice: Counsel: keep children away from the treated scalp and pillow (infant hair growth reported); topical 5-ARIs pass through skin.
source: clinical-men 3.1 (infants) and 10.2 table (women or children in the household); clinical-women 3.1 counsel.

treated.effect: removes dutasteride in the automatic offer only

boots-online-doctor.effect: recreational drugs: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged)

bestPractice: Record only. Counsel smokers that minoxidil solution and foam are flammable (do not apply while smoking). No product needs to be blocked for smoking or alcohol on the evidence in our files.
source: Flammability counsel (clinical-women 3.1). No smoking or alcohol restriction appears in the clinical files.

treated.effect: BMI > 35: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged)

ro.effect: not asked

bestPractice: Record weight as a baseline for oral minoxidil (rapid weight gain is a stop sign). Ask women about rapid weight loss and weight-loss injections (shedding trigger). No BMI gate.
source: clinical-men 11 stop rules; clinical-women 3.13 and 4.1 Q14, Q28.

dr-fox.effect: sexual side effects: removes finasteride and dutasteride products

boots-online-doctor.effect: current users: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) (amber)

happy-head.effect: flagged for the clinician (offer unchanged) 'critical'; dutasteride kept

bestPractice: Mood or persistent sexual effects: no 5-ARI (finasteride or dutasteride, oral or topical) without specialist review. Minor effects: clinician discussion.
source: MHRA warnings; effects may persist (clinical-men 10.1); topical is not a way round the warning (clinical-men 10.1 'What this means').

sons.effect: removes all minoxidil products (spray and capsule)

ro.effect: oral: removes oral minoxidil from recommendation

bestPractice: Ask what happened. Scalp irritation: switch to foam or consider oral. Heart, swelling or fainting on oral: no oral minoxidil.
source: clinical-men 11 step 2 table and stop rules; clinical-women 4.1 Q32.

situation: No family history of hair loss

ro.effect: men not asked; women none

bestPractice: Not a stop. Women: the licensed minoxidil SmPC says 'not indicated' without family history, so the clinician confirms the pattern from photos and records why. Men: supports the diagnosis only.
source: clinical-women 3.1 ('licence limit that is easy to miss') and 4.1 Q17.
